title: God hates concupiscence without hating the regenerate person (Bellarmine duplex odium)
source_text: XXXI. Quin concedunt concupiscentiam, etiam qualis est in justificatis, esse rem quam Deus damnat atque odit. Ut autem istud concilient cum eo quod definit Tridentina Synodus, nempe in renatis Deum nihil odisse, distinguunt duplex in Deo odium; unum quod in personam redundat, alterum quod non redundat in personam. Priori modo dicunt Deum non odisse concupiscentiam quae reliqua est in renatis; quia non reddit personam in qua est Deo odiosam. Sed posteriori modo fatentur Deum odio habere concupiscentiam, quia res est Deo displicens, quamque Deus ex renatis sublatam vult, & auferendam curat, licet illa non obstet quominus persona fidelis Deo grata sit atque accepta. Non enim, inquit Bellarminus, apud quem est illa distinctio, Deus propter concupiscentiam, quae est in renatis, vult renatos damnare: sed potius vult concupiscentiam paulatim consumere, ut renati perfecte sanentur & liberentur. De Amissione gratiae, lib. 5. cap. 13. sub finem.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed they concede that concupiscence, even as it is in the justified, is a thing which God condemns and hates. But that they may reconcile this with what the Tridentine Synod defines, namely that God hates nothing in the regenerate, they distinguish a twofold hatred in God; one which redounds upon the person, another which does not redound upon the person. In the former way they say God does not hate the concupiscence that is left in the regenerate; because it does not render the person in whom it is hateful to God. But in the latter way they confess God holds concupiscence in hatred, because it is a thing displeasing to God, which God wills removed from the regenerate and takes care to have taken away, although it does not prevent the faithful person from being pleasing and acceptable to God. For, says Bellarmine, in whom that distinction is found, God does not will to damn the regenerate because of the concupiscence that is in them: but rather wills gradually to consume the concupiscence, that the regenerate may be perfectly healed and freed. On the Loss of Grace, book 5, chapter 13, toward the end.
pass_b_english: Rome: God hates remaining concupiscence as a displeasing thing, yet not with person-damning hatred (Trent 'hates nothing in the regenerate').
Bellarmine: God consumes it gradually so the regenerate are healed—not damned for it.
